I am 63 years old and I have farmed these same 6 mu in Quzhou County since I was a young bride. My husband passed away five years ago, so now I manage the land myself, though my son comes back from the city to help with harvest. I never went to school, but I know this land better than any book. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Lao Wang, who has good luck with his crops.

It is almost October, so I will plant winter wheat on all 6 mu. I will buy improved wheat seed from the seed station — the same kind Lao Wang used last year, because his wheat stood up well to the wind and gave a good harvest. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed right after we cut the wheat in June. Everyone knows you cannot save corn seed; it grows poorly and stunted, so I buy fresh hybrid bags every year.

For fertilizer, I learned my lesson two years ago when I tried to save money and used less. The wheat turned yellow and thin, and I lost half a season. Now I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu for wheat, and about three-quarters of a bag per mu for corn. The young extension fellow says it is too much, but I would rather waste a little money than risk a bad crop. I also topdress urea when the wheat starts jointing, and again for the corn when it gets tall and starts flowering.

Irrigation costs me dearly because the electricity for the well keeps getting more expensive, but wheat needs water four times — once before winter, once at jointing, once when the heads come out, and once when the grains are filling. The corn needs three good waterings, especially when the tassels and silks appear. If I skip one, the yield drops badly.

For tillage, I hire the tractor with the rotary tiller for the wheat field in the fall. But after we cut the wheat in early June, we have only two or three days before the corn must go in, so we plant with no-tillage straight into the stubble. There is no time to plough.

I spray pesticides three times on the wheat — once for weeds before planting, once for bugs in spring, and once for the rust disease that comes when it gets humid. For corn, twice is enough, mainly for weeds and the corn borer that gets in the stalk. I expect about 480 kg per mu of wheat, and about 550 kg per mu of corn. Last year was similar. If the weather holds, that is enough to feed us and sell a little for cash.
